newsitem.title: UK: Iraq oil may boost Atlantic arrivals rush-analyst.
newsitem.headline: Iraq oil may boost Atlantic arrivals rush-analyst.

text.p: A hurried resumption of Iraqi oil exports could result in a "troublesome" boost to already-rising Atlantic basin crude arrivals in August, analyst Oil Movements said on Friday.

A rush of exports by Baghdad to meet a U.N. timetable to export $1 billion worth by early September under the "oil-for-food" programme could coincide with a flood of westbound arrivals into the Atlantic, the weekly said.
"The exit of Iraqi crude from the market last month was barely noticed in cold statistical tersm," the weekly said.

"But the re-entry could be more troublesome. A rush to meet the U.N. timetable might just coincide with rising arrivals of long haul Middle East (cargoes) to the Atlantic basin, being widely advertised for next month."

Oil Movements said westbound oil in transit from the Middle East rose to 146 million barrels in the week to July 13, compared to between 136 million and 140 million barrels in the weeks to June 22 and 29.
Total oil in transit east and westbound from the Middle East rose to around 308 million barrels in the week to July 20 from 289 million and 297 million in the weeks to June 22 and 29.
Total crude at sea worldwide fell to 435 million barrels in the week to July 20 from 440 million the previous week but is running above the 414 million and 411 million in the weeks to June 22 and 29.
"Latest figures for westbound oil show early signs of recovery, with an important bearing on the supply/demand balance in the Atlantic basin for the weeks ahead," Oil Movements said.
It said the Brent-Dubai crude price spread widened in early June when westbound Middle East cargoes were falling and eastbound cargoes were rising.
It added "On recent precedent, a rising volume of westbound oil runs along with a narrowing price spread."
